key_insight: DxToniaNet estimated expert-rated leg dystonia severity from clinical videos of children with cerebral palsy, with a reported mean absolute error of 1.71 points on a 0–40 scale.
clinical_relevance: Video-based severity estimation could support more consistent assessments in clinical care and trials, but clinical utility requires further validation.
method: Used OpenPose to track bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates during a seated hand open-close task.
Calculated 69 normalized movement variance and amplitude features.
Trained a neural network using five-fold cross-validation at Center 1, then tested it independently at Center 2.
evidence_signal: The retrospective study analyzed videos from 298 children across two centers; among videos showing dystonia, reported estimation error was below the 4-point clinically important difference, with 90–94% accuracy distinguishing videos whose expert scores differed by more than 4 points.
watch_item: Model development and testing included only videos showing dystonia, so performance for detecting its absence or across other tasks and settings remains uncertain.
paper_title: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy
